_comment: The 46 cells of the Periodic Table of Agent Invariants, as DATA. Extracted verbatim from the `families` literal that used to live inside opensentience.org/invariants.html at INV-R7.3. The page is now GENERATED from this file: `node opensentience.org/_invariants/build/build.mjs`. Two gates (check-mosaic.mjs, check-claim-ledger.mjs) used to eval() their subject out of a web page; they read this instead. Authored prose lives here; every count, register, status cross-check and ledger join is DERIVED at build time and may not be written down.

_fields.status: The AUTHORED cell status. Six tokens, distinct from CLAIM_LEDGER.json `_statuses` — see axes.json `statuses`.
_fields.kind: Semantic kind, from mosaic/occupancy.json `kind_vocabulary.declared`. NOT duplicated here.
_fields.kind_source: declared = assigned by a round that reviewed it. authored = assigned when the table was regrouped, on the cell's own stated source, and COUNTED on the page.
_fields.protocol_group: The pre-v0.8 grouping: which spec folder owns the cell. Kept as a sub-label — it is real, it is just not a structural axis.
_fields.tier: machine | property | impl. Presence means an evidence anchor exists; absence means none does.
_fields.register: NOT A FIELD. Derived by build.mjs from tier + the CLAIM_LEDGER.json join + status.
_fields.kind_why: Required when kind_source is "authored": the line of the cell's own record the assignment is read off. An authored kind with no `kind_why` is refused by the build.
_fields.witnesses: Runnable evidence for a cell whose ledger claims do not already name one. Paths are resolved on disk by the build (R12) — a witness that is present and dead is the round-3 defect.
_fields.witness_note: Optional prose beside `witnesses`: what the witness actually decides.
_fields.evidence_absent: Required on a DECIDED cell that has neither a proof page nor any witness. States why, so the absence is declared rather than silent.

cells.label: Cyclicity
cells.kind_why: source: the largest SCC of a directed graph — a property of the carrier's shape
cells.title: κ — Cyclicity
cells.tagline: When the graph has feedback, flat reasoning fails.
cells.desc: Measures the minimum bidirectional cut across the largest strongly connected component. κ = 0 means the region is a DAG and one-pass retrieval suffices; κ > 0 means feedback loops survive any decomposition and deliberation is required.
cells.extra: Proved across 1,926,351 finite directed systems with zero counterexamples. Categorically, κ is the obstruction to trace-free decomposition in a traced symmetric monoidal category (JSV). CORRECTION 2026-08-23: κ does NOT carry the federation obstruction of entry 36, and a previous version of this table's write-up claimed it did. κ is defined on DIRECTED graphs via the largest SCC; constraint edges are symmetric, so every orientation of a constraint carrier is arbitrary. The diamond a→b, a→c, b→d, c→d has all SCCs trivial and κ = 0, yet its undirected 4-cycle is split across two sites and fidelity fails. The federation carrier is entry 45, κ_split.

cells.label: Persistence
cells.title: β — Persistence
cells.tagline: Which features survive the next consolidation.
cells.desc: Normalized rank over a filtration of consolidation epochs. A feature with high β has persisted across many epochs and is durable enough to promote into semantic memory. Low β means provisional, subject to pruning.
cells.extra: Replaces recency- and frequency-based pruning with a principled durability measure. The formal handle on what makes memory compound rather than accumulate-and-stale.

cells.label: Tree-likeness
cells.title: τ — Tree-likeness
cells.tagline: How hierarchical is this neighborhood?
cells.desc: Positive when the neighborhood is approximately acyclic and hierarchical. High τ identifies regions where a single fault cascades exponentially through dependents.
cells.extra: Composes with ρ to authorize redundant-execution mode rather than deliberation — failures should be tolerated by replication, not resolved by argument.

cells.label: Curvature
cells.title: ρ — Discrete Ricci curvature
cells.tagline: Tree-like, grid-like, or sphere-like?
cells.desc: Local discrete Ricci curvature of the neighborhood. Negative = tree-like (hierarchical authority natural). Zero = grid-like (peer-to-peer). Positive = sphere-like / cycle-rich (collective authority natural).
cells.extra: Each curvature regime warrants a different governance mode. The same knowledge graph contains regions of all three.

cells.label: Mobility
cells.title: μ — Reachable-state mobility
cells.tagline: How many futures does this position admit?
cells.desc: A measure of how many distinct downstream states the current sub-graph can reach. Chess analog: piece activity. Low μ means the position is locked; high μ means it is fertile.
cells.extra: Suggested by the chess analogy — the agent equivalent of squares-of-influence. Not yet formalized.

cells.label: Tempo
cells.title: Tempo invariant (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Who is forcing whom?
cells.desc: Chess has tempo — the most underrated structural variable. The agent equivalent measures whether the system is reactive (responding to inputs) or proactive (setting the agenda).
cells.extra: PULSE gestures at this temporally but does not formalize it as an invariant. Open research question.

cells.label: Opson
cells.title: ω — Opson · opportunity-volume
cells.tagline: Money as work-I-don't-have-to-do, formalized.
cells.desc: A counterfactual-reachability token: ω is earned by an agent whose contribution provably expanded the action-space of downstream agents. Concretely, ω(a) = |R(G ∪ a) ∖ R(G)|, where R(G) is the set of valid plans reachable in the graph before agent a's contribution, and R(G ∪ a) the set after. Closes the loop the user opened in earlier conversation: "money = work I don't have to do." The thing that doesn't have to be done is the planning effort that a's contribution now makes free.
cells.extra: ω composes with β: contributions whose reachability-deltas persist across many epochs (high β · high ω) are durable infrastructure. Contributions with high ω but low β are bubbles — they look transformative briefly, then evaporate. The intersection is what merits long-tail royalty claims (see θ, entry 43).
cells.formal:
ω(a) := |R(G ∪ {a}) ∖ R(G)|

Conserved under: graph-isomorphism on R
Minted on: net positive reachability-delta
Burned on: deletion of a from G without preserving R
Composes with: β (persistence), ε (delegation)

cells.label: Split cyclicity
cells.title: κₛ — Split cyclicity
cells.tagline: Not whether the carrier has cycles — whether a cycle crosses a boundary.
cells.desc: κₛ = 0 exactly when EVERY SITE'S EDGE SET IS A SEPARATOR OF THE CYCLE MATROID of the bipartite incidence graph — equivalently, the site colouring is constant on every matroid component, equivalently the matroid is the direct sum of its site restrictions. One carrier covers every arity: for binary constraints the incidence graph is the subdivision of the constraint multigraph. The index itself is Σ over the blocks of max(0, |sites(B)| − 1), and only its ZERO SET is claimed.
cells.extra: Zero-set proved: a split cycle is 2-connected and therefore lies inside one block, which then carries ≥ 2 sites; conversely any two edges of a block lie on a common cycle, so a block with two sites has a split cycle. Checked against brute-force enumeration of every simple cycle on 117,648 federations, 0 mismatches. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: only the zero set. The magnitude Σ max(0, |sites(B)| − 1) is one defensible aggregation of several and is a declared index, not a canonical invariant. NOT ordinary cycle rank: b₁ = |E| − |V| + c was the first proposed repair and it is wrong in the direction that matters — a single site holding a triangle has b₁ = 1 and no split cycle, so b₁ reports an obstruction the federation theorem says is absent. b₁ and κₛ disagree on 1,440 of the 15,624 four-variable federations. ROUND 3 — the zero set is a standard matroid statement, and that is what retired the two-carrier machinery: matroid components are the classes of 'lie on a common circuit' (Oxley §4.1), a separator is a union of components (§4.2), and for a cycle matroid the components are the block edge sets. Verified on both carriers against independent brute force. THE MAGNITUDE QUESTION MOVED but did not close. FIVE declared indices — impure-component count; Σ max(0, |sites(B)| − 1); minimum recolourings; minimum carrier deletions to purify; and the partition-lattice gap |sites| − #components of the site-conflict graph, which is the minimum number of site merges and the only one with a matroid meaning — are pairwise distinct on explicit federations, all ten pairs separated. That shows the theorem FIXES no magnitude. It does not show that none is canonical: 'canonical' is not defined here, so that is not a proposition anything above could refute, and the round-3 research pass's 'canonical magnitude refuted' is an overclaim. Sharper evidence that none of them is the invariant: the zero set AGREES between the binary constraint multigraph and its incidence-graph subdivision while the MAGNITUDES DO NOT — minimum recolouring reads 2 on a three-site triangle and 4 on its subdivision. The class is named deliberately: what is proved is invariance under that ONE normalization, not under some unspecified family of carrier transformations, and 'carrier-invariant' should not be published as a general phrase until such a family is defined.

cells.label: Conflict
cells.title: σ — Derived conflict
cells.tagline: Local agreement, global disagreement.
cells.desc: The SCOPE-derived conflict predicate. Given regions and claims under deterministic overlap rules, σ > 0 when claims of incompatible strength overlap within the same frame.
cells.extra: Originally framed as sheaf cohomology (H¹ obstruction). Dropped in favor of constraint logic — the operational primitive that actually ships. Same computation, less apparatus.

cells.label: Coherence
cells.title: χ — Frame-transform coherence
cells.tagline: Do cross-region morphisms compose?
cells.desc: When SCOPE's vocabulary v0.2 introduces transforms between heterogeneous region kinds (viewport ↔ document span, grid ↔ geojson), χ measures when those transforms compose coherently.
cells.extra: Open question for SCOPE v0.2. Has well-developed mathematical machinery if the cohomological framing is revived for transforms specifically.

cells.label: Mobility-spatial
cells.title: Spatial mobility (unnamed)
cells.tagline: How much of the environment is reachable?
cells.desc: Spatial analog of μ — measures how much of an embodied agent's environment is reachable within budget. Distinct from logical-graph mobility because it involves physical / virtual locomotion constraints.
cells.extra: Open. Needed for GeoFleetic / body-os spatial reasoning.

cells.label: Phase order
cells.kind_why: desc: "the five canonical phases occur in a partial order that no compliant loop may violate"
cells.title: π — Phase ordering
cells.tagline: Retrieve → route → act → learn → consolidate.
cells.desc: PULSE's first invariant: the five canonical phases occur in a partial order that no compliant loop may violate. Verified by the 12-test conformance suite.
cells.extra: One of seven invariants in PULSE v0.1. Catalog of the others is in the os-pulse repository; surfacing them on pulse.opensentience.org is on the immediate roadmap.

cells.label: Idempotence
cells.title: ι — Token idempotence
cells.tagline: Replaying a token must not double-fire.
cells.desc: Each of the five canonical cross-loop tokens (TopologyContext, DeliberationResult, OutcomeSignal, ReputationUpdate, ConsolidationEvent) is idempotent under retry. Failure-recovery without state corruption.
cells.extra: One of PULSE's seven invariants. Documented in conformance test #4.

cells.label: Cadence
cells.title: ψ — Cadence honesty
cells.tagline: Declared rate matches observed rate.
cells.desc: PULSE manifests declare a cadence type (continuous, periodic, event-driven, on-demand, batch, hybrid). ψ verifies that observed behavior matches the declaration within tolerance.
cells.extra: One of PULSE's seven invariants. Enables PRISM to evaluate loop behavior against its own contract.

cells.label: Tempo-temporal
cells.title: Initiative (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Who advanced the loop?
cells.desc: Distinct from PULSE's phase ordering: this would measure who/what advanced the loop on the last cycle — agent, environment, schedule, external system.
cells.extra: Closely related to topological tempo but operationalized over PULSE phases rather than graph topology.

cells.label: No cycles
cells.kind_why: source: "DAG enforcement" — acyclicity of the authority graph
cells.title: ⊘ — No cycles in authority graph
cells.tagline: Delegation is acyclic by construction.
cells.desc: The authority graph (who can delegate to whom) admits no cycles. Prevents privilege loops and infinite delegation chains. Enforced at write time, not detected at read time.
cells.extra: One of four Delegatic security invariants. The structural opposite of κ — where the knowledge graph welcomes cycles, the authority graph forbids them.

cells.label: Monotonic
cells.title: ⊆ — Monotonic inheritance
cells.tagline: Children cannot exceed their parents.
cells.desc: Child contexts inherit a strict subset of parent permissions. A team cannot grant its members capabilities the team itself does not hold. Attempted privilege escalation is rejected at write time.
cells.extra: One of four Delegatic security invariants. Provides the structural guarantee that auditing the root tells you everything possible downstream.

cells.label: Deny default
cells.kind_why: source: "Capability theory" — permitted only if an explicit grant exists
cells.title: ⊥ — Deny by default
cells.tagline: Absence of grant equals refusal.
cells.desc: An action is permitted only if an explicit grant exists. Silence is refusal. Eliminates ambient authority and makes the policy surface explicit.
cells.extra: One of four Delegatic security invariants. Standard capability-system discipline applied to agent governance.

cells.label: Append-only
cells.title: ⊕ — Append-only audit
cells.tagline: History cannot be rewritten.
cells.desc: Every authority decision is logged to an append-only audit stream. Past entries are immutable. Provides the structural basis for post-incident review and external compliance.
cells.extra: One of four Delegatic security invariants. The audit trail is the proof that the other three invariants were never violated.

cells.label: Non-laundering
cells.kind_why: statement: a change of representation may never manufacture permission; authority: "refuse"
cells.title: Λ — Non-laundering
cells.tagline: A change of representation may never manufacture permission.
cells.desc: Normalization, coercion, defaulting, encoding and decoding may PRESERVE or REDUCE what a claim asserts — never increase it. Evidence that is missing, unknown, malformed or unverifiable must floor to refusal: never to a wildcard, never to an empty set, never to a benign identity value, and never to a privileged algebraic term.
cells.extra: Found by generalizing over four defects that looked unrelated and were the same mistake. (1) An ABSENT contract end defaulted to '*', so an assembly that declared no interface received the most permissive one in the algebra — CD1–CD5. (2) A MALFORMED end was filtered of the parts the parser could not read and the residue returned as a declaration, usually the empty set, and ∅ ⊆ X holds for every X — CD10/CD11. (3) A MALFORMED semantic value floored to V0(), the benign identity: feasible, acyclic, no conflict, LIVE — CX7. A fuzzer asking only 'never throw' was fully satisfied by that. (4) An ordinary brick acquired IDENTITY privilege by declaring a field, because serialisability had been mistaken for authenticity — CD12. Each fix changed the representation and left the meta-error; the invariant is what survives all four.
cells.source: Generalized from CD1–CD5, CD10–CD12, CX7, VX1–VX5
cells.witness_note: The CD, CX and VX families constitute it. Each was written before its fix and observed to fail; the build fails if one starts passing for the wrong reason.

cells.label: Nexus
cells.title: ν — Nexus · mutual-credit peer settlement
cells.tagline: Currency that only exists between two agents in the act of exchange.
cells.desc: A bilateral ledger primitive: when agent A pays agent B in ν, A's balance with B goes negative by exactly the amount B's goes positive. ν is not held — it exists only as the asymmetric trace of a transaction between two specific parties. Total supply across the network is always exactly zero by construction; inflation is structurally impossible. Adapts the WIR / LETS / Sardex mutual-credit pattern (Lietaer 2001) to agent settlement.
cells.extra: ν composes with ⊕ (append-only) for non-repudiation and with ε (epistemic delegation) for credit-limit setting. Agents accumulating persistent negative balances are flagged as net consumers; persistent positive balances mark net producers. The ledger is the reputation system. Eighty-year empirical track record at population scale in the Swiss WIR (Stodder 2009).
cells.formal:
ν(A,B,t) ∈ ℝ
∀A,B: ν(A,B,t) = −ν(B,A,t)
∑_{A,B} ν(A,B,t) ≡ 0   ∀t

Conserved: pairwise sum (always zero)
Minted on: transaction (only)
Burned on: settlement-to-zero
Composes with: ⊕, ε

cells.label: Episteme
cells.title: ε — Episteme · delegation-bound trust receipt
cells.tagline: Trust held, not value owned.
cells.desc: Earned by being delegated to: when A grants B authority over a bounded resource pool, B earns ε equal to the bounded value of the grant, scaled by the parent's own ε balance (recursive trust). ε is non-transferable — it represents capacity for trust, not transferable claim — but ε is redeemable for other tokens (ν, θ) at a rate that depends on the trust's age and honored-reliability ratio. Long-held, well-honored delegations redeem at a premium.
cells.extra: Extends ⊆ (monotonic inheritance) by making the act of delegation itself an asset on the delegate's balance sheet. Solves the reputation-as-currency problem without making reputation directly transferable (which is the failure mode of most reputation tokens). ε ages well; it compounds when honored, decays when violated, and is the only entry that explicitly does both.
cells.formal:
ε(B) := Σ_{A: A delegates to B} grant(A,B) · (ε(A) / ε_max) · h(B,t)
where h(B,t) ∈ [0,1] is the honored-reliability ratio

Non-transferable: ε(B) cannot become ε(C) by transfer
Redeemable: ε → ν, ε → θ at rate r(age, h)
Conserved: total ε is bounded by aggregate-grant volume
Composes with: ⊆, ⊕, θ
cells.source: Capability theory + reputation systems · cf. EigenTrust

cells.label: Convergence
cells.title: Argument convergence (unnamed)
cells.tagline: When does the argument settle?
cells.desc: An invariant that measures whether deliberation among multiple agents is approaching a fixed point, oscillating, or diverging. Authorizes either continued deliberation or escalation to a sealing authority.
cells.extra: Open. Likely involves measuring entropy reduction across rounds.

cells.label: Dissent durability
cells.title: Vindicated dissent (β × σ)
cells.tagline: When disagreement is structural, not noise.
cells.desc: Composition of β and σ: when σ > 0 across many consolidation epochs (high β on the obstruction class), the disagreement is durable. Authorizes preserve-dissent operation rather than forced consensus.
cells.extra: Already implied by the κ/σ/β composition but not yet a named first-class invariant in OS-003.

cells.label: Seal integrity
cells.title: Seal integrity (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Can a sealed outcome be reopened?
cells.desc: Once a deliberation is sealed, under what conditions may it be reopened? An invariant defining the cryptographic and procedural conditions for re-litigation.
cells.extra: Open. Related to common-law precedent: a sealed outcome is precedent until the σ-class beneath it changes.

cells.label: Salience persistence
cells.title: Salience persistence (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Does what was important stay important?
cells.desc: An attention-layer analog of β: which foci of attention persist across cycles vs which decay. Authorizes promotion from working memory to long-term focus.
cells.extra: Open. The chess analog is which threats remain live across multiple moves.

cells.label: Focus coherence
cells.title: Focus coherence (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Do the things being attended to fit together?
cells.desc: When multiple foci are active, do they form a coherent attention plan or compete? Measures whether the agent's attention is plan-like or fragmented.
cells.extra: Open. Closely related to σ but on the attention layer rather than the knowledge layer.

cells.label: Attention budget
cells.title: Attention-budget conservation (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Attention is finite and tracked.
cells.desc: An invariant that conserves total attention budget across foci. Adding focus to one region requires withdrawing from another. Prevents attention inflation.
cells.extra: Open. The chess analog is that you cannot calculate everything; calculation is itself a resource.

cells.label: Phos
cells.title: φ — Phos · attention-credit currency
cells.tagline: Earned by directing thought productively. Burned by asking others to think.
cells.desc: An attention-credit token. φ is minted when an agent productively spends deliberation cycles (a κ-invocation that yields a downstream-useful artifact) and burned when an agent asks other agents to think on its behalf. Total φ in circulation is bounded by the system's per-epoch compute budget, so the supply is hard-capped at the physical scarcity (not a fiat decision). This is the closest token to the user's original "money = freedom" intuition: holding φ means holding directable cognitive bandwidth.
cells.extra: φ is the short-cycle currency of the substrate — it's what flows moment-to-moment as agents trade attention. Composes with ψ (cadence honesty) for verification: an agent claiming a φ-mint must show a manifest-honored deliberation. Compute-burn provenance is the φ analog of energy proof-of-work — except the work is structurally tied to the substrate's actual function, not arbitrary hashing.
cells.formal:
φ_mint(a, t) := work(a, t) · indicator{β(output(a,t)) > θ_β}
φ_burn(a, t) := compute_requested(a → other, t)
∑_a φ(a, t) ≤ compute_budget(t)   ∀t

Conserved: bounded by compute budget
Minted on: productive κ-invocation with β-mark on output
Burned on: delegated deliberation request
Composes with: ψ, κ, β

cells.label: Escalation monotonicity
cells.title: Escalation monotonicity (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Stronger models do not make things worse.
cells.desc: FALSE in its universal form and replaced by TWO distinct certificates, which must not be conflated. (1) QUALITY EXPECTATION: a paired mean-difference certificate, E[q_H − q_L] ≥ 0 on task family F. (2) ESCALATION TAIL SAFETY: an (η,δ)-domination certificate, P[q_H < q_L] ≤ η at confidence 1−δ. Neither implies the other — a model that loses slightly on 10% of tasks and wins hugely on the rest passes (1) and fails (2) at η = 1%.
cells.extra: The universal claim is dead structurally, not just empirically: quantifying over all task families includes singletons, so monotonicity for every family is equivalent to POINTWISE domination on every task, and pointwise domination is a partial order that inverse scaling shows is not total on any natural model set. So no global capability ranking licenses escalation; a per-family certificate does. SAMPLE COST: zero observed violations in n tasks certify (η,δ) when (1−η)^n ≤ δ, so n ≈ ln(1/δ)/η — about 299 tasks at η = 1%, δ = 5%, which is practical. The mean-difference certificate is cheap only for large margins: a 1-point margin on a 0–100 scale needs ~6·10⁴ tasks. EVALUATOR NOISE IS THE REAL THREAT: with a single judge flipping comparisons at rate p ≥ 1%, the zero-violation certificate issues about 5% of the time even when domination genuinely holds, so the sample budget must declare judges-per-task alongside n, or η must absorb p. η composes additively along an escalation chain by a union bound, which makes certificate slack itself a depletable resource — the same affine algebra as entry 25.
cells.authority: escalate (per family, under a declared evaluator protocol)
cells.source: Inverse Scaling Prize (McKenzie et al. 2023) · Wei et al. 2022 (U-shaped) · binomial confidence bounds

cells.label: Cost conservation
cells.hypothesis: The meter is faithful — every recorded debit bounds an incurred cost. The ledger algebra is proved; nothing in it certifies that its debits match real spend, and the metered process can lie, crash mid-charge, or be billed out-of-band.
cells.title: Cost-budget conservation (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Spend matches declared budget.
cells.desc: Total cost across a task is bounded by the declared budget. Overruns trigger explicit reauthorization rather than silent debt. Implemented as the affine ledger at rung 8 of the box-and-box arithmetic ladder: C1 conservation (Σ invariant under transfer), C2 no overdraft, C4 linearity, C6 monotone depletion, CB1 exhaustion ⇒ infeasible — which is literally this cell's declared authority — and CB2 additive composition along a pipeline.
cells.extra: NOT missing, and it was marked missing here while passing property tests in this tree at 2,000 trials each. resource.mjs, laws C1–C10 and CB1–CB4. What is not proved is meter faithfulness, so the residual question is sharper than the original cell: under what conditions does a recorded debit provably bound an incurred cost? Note also that reversibility is a FEATURE here and a defect for entry 27b: a token refund is legitimate, and the same operation on an information budget is the 'reset ε' error. That is why the ledger now carries a resource kind, and why a cell citing it must say which kind it means.
cells.source: Linear logic (Girard 1987) · affine ledger · Good 1971 / Russell–Wefald 1989 (metareasoning)

cells.label: Capability floor
cells.title: Capability floor (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Downshift preserves a minimum.
cells.desc: When the system downshifts to a lighter model, a defined minimum capability is preserved. Prevents catastrophic degradation in cost-saving mode.
cells.extra: Open. Defines what 'lighter' actually means.

cells.label: Demurra
cells.title: δ — Demurra · demurrage operational currency
cells.tagline: Tokens that decay if they aren't spent on substrate work.
cells.desc: Operational currency with Gesell-style demurrage: every δ-unit loses ρ% of its value per PULSE epoch unless spent on σ-resolution, κ-deliberation, or β-promotion. Hoarding is structurally taxed. Adapts the Wörgl scrip (Gesell 1916; Wörgl 1932) and modern Japanese Peanuts (1%/month) to agent operation. Forces circulation, which forces multi-agent collaboration — an agent earning δ and sitting on it is wasting it; an agent immediately spending it on a resolution is converting time-decaying tokens into permanent β-artifacts that mint θ.
cells.extra: δ is income; θ (entry 43) is savings. Agents naturally flow δ → β-work → θ-claims, which is the substrate-economic equivalent of the Lietaer pattern "local currency for circulation, hard currency for storage." δ is the friction-against-hoarding that keeps a Lietaer-style multi-currency ecosystem moving.
cells.formal:
δ(a, t+1) := δ(a, t) · (1 − ρ)   if not spent in epoch t
ρ ≈ 0.05–0.10 per epoch (calibration parameter)

Conserved: no — δ is intentionally lossy
Minted on: completion of σ-resolution or κ-deliberation
Burned on: spending OR decay (the design point)
Composes with: σ, κ, β, θ

cells.label: Grava
cells.title: γ — Grava · compute-backed reserve
cells.tagline: The hard floor under everything else.
cells.desc: A reserve asset backed by an actual compute claim: each γ-unit is redeemable for a specified quantity of GPU-hours, context-window tokens, or storage. γ is the agent-economy analog of a commodity standard, but the commodity is the actual substrate scarcity rather than gold. Where δ inflates/deflates with circulation, γ has a hard physical floor — the underlying compute either exists or doesn't.
cells.extra: γ functions as the treasury asset on agent and fleet balance sheets. Agents pay each other in δ, φ, and ν day-to-day, but they hold γ as reserves against shocks. This is the substrate equivalent of central-bank reserves vs. M1, except the reserve is denominated in the physical scarcity rather than in another fiat. Resolves the Lietaer-Ulanowicz "window of vitality" tradeoff by giving the economy a fixed-redemption anchor that prevents the multi-currency stack from drifting into pure speculation.
cells.formal:
γ(a) := compute_claim(a)  ∈  {gpu_hours, context_tokens, storage_bytes}
redemption: γ → physical resource at fixed rate r

Conserved: bounded by total provisioned compute
Minted on: compute provisioning (substrate operator action)
Burned on: redemption to physical resource
Composes with: δ (reserve ratio), θ (settlement collateral)

cells.label: Holdout containment
cells.observer_model: UNDECLARED for the real runner. The in-tree battery closes the file/direct-read channel only; timing, resource-usage and reference-subject channels are untested. A two-run non-interference statement is meaningless until this names what the low observer can see, and a checker built against a MODEL of the runner does not discharge it for the runner.
cells.title: Holdout containment (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Test set never leaks — the data channel.
cells.desc: The holdout scenarios never appear, in any form, in any system the benchmark evaluates. This is the DATA-containment half of what this cell used to ask for as a single property.
cells.extra: Enforced in-tree by the TRVM P4.7.1 falsifier battery: the reveal boundary did not exist — a candidate could read all of H1…H10 — and the gate moved inside the frozen experiment_digest so a mutable wrapper cannot drop it. Closes the DIRECT-READ channel only. Timing, resource-usage and reference-subject channels are untested, and a non-interference property needs a declared observer model before it can claim more. The kind is marked Flow? because a full two-run non-interference statement — vary the holdout, hold candidate-visible inputs fixed, require indistinguishability — is a hyperproperty whose refutation is a PAIR of runs, which none of the eight kinds can express. It stays provisional until an executable two-run witness exists; the property proved today is the narrower containment boundary, which Structural × Authority does cover. ROUND 3 — the two-run OBJECT now exists and the KIND question is still open, and those are different things. What is settled: the strong reading is a 2-safety property relative to a declared observer and declassification policy, its refutation is a pair of low-equivalent runs, and self-composition (Barthe–D'Argenio–Rezk 2004) reduces it to ordinary safety on the product system. That is recorded as `relational_arity: 2` rather than as a ninth kind, because 'a reduction to single-trace safety exists' is NOT a proof that Flow cannot be a semantic kind — many semantic properties have such reductions. The ontology inference was made in round 3 and does not follow. The likelier shape is that the table needs ORTHOGONAL AXES — semantic kind × run arity (1, 2, k, distribution) × quantification mode × observer/policy × enforcement authority — and 'Flow: yes or no' is the wrong question to force. Flow? stays provisional.
cells.source: ML methodology · non-interference (Clarkson–Schneider 2010) for the stronger form

cells.label: Holdout budget
cells.hypothesis: An i.i.d. holdout (required for (ε,δ) currencies — Rogers–Roth–Smith–Thakkar 2016), a declared composable currency, and 27a containment: the meter is faithful only if every holdout→candidate flow passes through it. If PRISM's scenarios share generation seeds they are not i.i.d. and the guarantee needs pure DP or a different argument.
cells.title: Holdout information budget (unnamed)
cells.tagline: The score is the leak — meter it, cap it, and never refund it.
cells.desc: The information about the holdout released to candidates is metered on an affine ledger with an ABSORBING sink (laws C1, C2, C6, CB1, plus C9/C10/CB4) in a composable currency — zCDP ρ, Rényi DP at fixed order, pure ε, or max-information bits. The cap is set from holdout size, tolerance and confidence by the transfer theorem; exhaustion ⇒ no further evaluation admissible.
cells.extra: This cell exists because the original entry 27 was satisfiable by a system whose holdout is already destroyed: a holdout can be overfit to uselessness by adaptive querying with no holdout data ever crossing the boundary. The destruction channel is the SCORE. CORRECTION 2026-08-23: the claim that this 'falls out of the existing ledger without changing the algebra' was wrong, and an executable witness shows why — spending the whole budget closed the gate, a transfer back out of the sink re-opened it, and C1 and C2 both still held, so no existing law objected. It needed a new law. The law is sink MONOTONICITY, not a ban on credit: moving previously-unspent budget out of the treasury is allocation and stays legal, because spending 5 of a cap of 10 does not forbid the other 5. A second correction: differential privacy does not compose quadratically. Advanced composition is O(ε√k) — TIGHTER than the additive kε, which remains a valid bound — and zCDP, RDP at fixed order and max-information all compose exactly additively, so an additive ledger is the right shape after all. CORRECTION 2026-08-24: the C10 cap reached the PRIMITIVE and not the GATE. `feasible` was a pure balance check, so with a cap of 6, a sink at 5 and an account holding 10 it said GO on a spend `transfer` was already committed to refusing — a decision layer answering yes over a primitive answering no, which is worse than either answer alone. No law objected because no law compared them. Both now consult ONE admissibility predicate; CB5 asserts the equivalence and CB6 asserts that no preflighted path (`use`, `repair`) can hand back INFEASIBLE dressed as a ledger. The general form is the lesson: A NEW INVARIANT IS NOT FINISHED WHEN THE PRIMITIVE THAT STATES IT ENFORCES IT — every other path deciding the same question has to be pointed at the same predicate. Separately, C10's 'declared, IMMUTABLE cap' was immutable only in a comment; `kind` and `cap` are now frozen (C11) and BALANCES ARE NOT, which is a declared boundary and not an oversight: a Ledger is a value, not a capability handle. Witness: scripts/check-irreversible-ledger.mjs §3, §4.
cells.source: Dwork–Feldman–Hardt–Pitassi–Reingold–Roth 2015 · Bun–Steinke 2016 (zCDP) · Mironov 2017 (RDP) · Feldman–Zrnic 2021 (fully adaptive privacy filter)

cells.label: Adversarial monotonicity
cells.title: Adversarial monotonicity (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Harder scenarios produce lower scores on weak systems.
cells.desc: When the benchmark generates a harder scenario, weak systems score lower on it. Prevents the benchmark from drifting toward scenarios that happen to favor incumbents.
cells.extra: Open. Necessary for the self-improving loop to not become a self-flattering loop.

cells.label: Anti-saturation
cells.title: Anti-saturation (unnamed)
cells.tagline: The benchmark gets harder as systems improve.
cells.desc: An invariant requiring that the median scenario difficulty rise as median system score rises. Operationalizes the principle that a useful benchmark cannot saturate.
cells.extra: Open. The structural reason LongMemEval saturated and PRISM should not.

cells.label: Tithon
cells.title: θ — Tithon · settlement / redemption invariant
cells.tagline: The bridge from internal economy to real-world capital.
cells.desc: The auditable invariant that maps internal token flow (ν, ε, δ, φ, ω, γ) to external USD settlement against actual customer revenue. θ-minting requires (a) verified β-mark on the underlying artifact, (b) σ-resolution audit trail, (c) ⊕-logged customer-USD inflow attributable to the work. Without θ, billars (the user's proposed denomination) are internal scrip; with θ, they are claims on a pro-rata share of customer USD at settlement. The Lietaer "complementary currency" pattern formalized as an auditable protocol.
cells.extra: θ is the single most consequential invariant for outside investors: it is the mechanism by which a real person buys a claim on the future θ-earnings of a specific agent or fleet, and is paid out in USD at settlement against actual revenue. This is closer to royalty securitization than to crypto. The denomination unit is the billar (B); one billar = one unit of θ at the current epoch's USD/θ rate. The exchange rate floats based on customer revenue / θ-minted ratio — a real exchange rate anchored to economic activity rather than speculation.
cells.formal:
θ_mint(a, work) := USD_in(customer, work) · share(a, work)
  where share(a, work) requires:
    β(output(work)) > θ_β       (persistence proof)
    ⊕(audit_trail(work)) = ✓    (append-only verified)
    σ-resolution log present

Redeemable: θ → USD at settlement
Denomination: 1 billar (B) = 1 unit of θ
Conserved: 1:1 against verified customer USD inflow
Composes with: ALL — θ is the settlement layer over the whole economy
cells.authority: redeem to USD · issue billar claim
cells.source: Lietaer 2001 · complementary currency settlement · revenue-share securities

cells.label: Continuity
cells.title: Embodiment continuity (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Body-state survives reload.
cells.desc: The agent's body-state (pose, viewport, focus, scroll, modal stack) is conserved across reload and reattachment. Without this, embodiment is just a session.
cells.extra: Open. Distinguishes embodiment from incarnation.

cells.label: Affordance honesty
cells.title: Affordance honesty (unnamed)
cells.tagline: The body advertises only what it can do.
cells.desc: Every affordance the body exposes to its driving agent must be one the body can actually execute. No phantom buttons. Prevents agents from confidently planning over fictional capabilities.
cells.extra: Open. Closely linked to OS-015 (Affordance Projection).

cells.label: Sensor-actuator coherence
cells.title: Sensor-actuator coherence (unnamed)
cells.tagline: What I see is what I just did.
cells.desc: Following an actuator command, the next sensor reading reflects the command's effect within bounded time. Prevents drift between agent's belief and body's actual state.
cells.extra: Open. The robotics literature has versions of this; the agent literature does not.

cells.label: Non-replay
cells.title: Credential non-replay (unnamed)
cells.tagline: A token used twice was used wrongly.
cells.desc: Standard cryptographic invariant adapted to agent credentials: a token consumed once cannot be consumed again. Prevents replay attacks on agent-to-agent authority transfer.
cells.extra: Open at OS-013. Off-the-shelf cryptographic primitive at the implementation layer.

cells.label: PII conservation
cells.title: PII conservation (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Sensitive data does not cross aggregation boundaries.
cells.desc: Telemetry and federated aggregation invariant: personally identifiable information present at the leaf is absent from the aggregate. Differential privacy at the protocol layer.
cells.extra: Open at OS-014 / OS-017. Implementable with established differential-privacy mechanisms. As written — 'PII present at the leaf is absent from the aggregate' — this is a single-output safety property and the eight kinds cover it. The STRONGER reading, that varying one leaf's PII leaves the aggregate indistinguishable, is non-interference: a 2-safety hyperproperty whose refutation is a PAIR of runs, which no single-trace kind can express. That reading shares its shape with entry 27a and is the case for a ninth kind, Flow. Marked provisional (Flow?) on the strength of two cells and no executable two-run witness; differential privacy is exactly the statistical relaxation of it.
cells.source: Differential privacy · non-interference (Clarkson–Schneider 2010) for the stronger form

cells.label: Causal order
cells.title: Causal-order preservation (unnamed)
cells.tagline: Aggregation does not reorder cause and effect.
cells.desc: When telemetry from multiple agents is unified, the causal order of related events is preserved in the unified stream. Concurrent events may be interleaved arbitrarily, but causally ordered pairs are not reordered.
cells.extra: Open at OS-014. Standard vector-clock / Lamport-timestamp territory at the implementation layer.

cells.label: Aggregation fidelity
cells.hypothesis: ROUTE 36a (AUTOMATIC) — the constraint template has a TRANSITIVE CORE: the automorphism group of the core of (D; Γ) acts transitively on it. That is the exact condition, decidable by enumerating endomorphisms, certified more cheaply (but not necessarily) by value symmetry, and equivalent to the older phrasings — some single domain value in every non-empty unary pp-definable projection, and no two DISJOINT such projections. Still UNKNOWN for the typed property-graph constraints FGAP would federate, and unlikely on value sorts: two literals on a sort already give two disjoint projections. '1-point amalgamation' is retired as a public name — it collides with the Fraïssé term — and no established name has been found for the equivalence itself. ROUTE 36b (CERTIFIED) — without any hypothesis on Γ, fidelity is DECIDED by exact unary separator projections passed up the block tree. That route is classical (Yannakakis 1981) and is the one that survives on realistic value sorts; what it does not yet have is a proof object a receiving site can check in both directions.
cells.title: Aggregation fidelity (unnamed)
cells.tagline: The federated view faithfully represents the union.
cells.desc: Fidelity — every site locally satisfiable ⟹ the federated union satisfiable — holds whenever (i) the constraint language Γ has 1-point amalgamation: any two satisfiable Γ-instances sharing exactly one variable have a satisfiable union; and (ii) no cycle of the union carrier is split across sites — κₛ = 0 (entry 45), reading cycles as Berge cycles for n-ary constraints. The universal form, with neither hypothesis, is FALSE.
cells.extra: The universal claim dies on three sites holding x≠y, y≠z, z≠x: each satisfiable, every pairwise overlap consistent, union unsatisfiable. The FIRST REPAIR ALSO DIED. 'No split cycle ⟹ fidelity' was tested over 240,000 random federations with zero counterexamples and is false anyway — false even when the carrier is a TREE, so cyclicity is not the obstruction at all for a general language. Site 1 holds v = 0, site 2 holds v = 1; the carrier is a path. The sweep could not have found this because every domain it sampled used eq/neq, whose symmetry group makes the lemma a short theorem — it was measuring a theorem, not probing a conjecture. The corrected statement is exact in both directions: split-cycle sufficiency holds for EVERY Γ-federation iff Γ has 1PA, since a 1PA failure is itself two sites meeting at a cut vertex with no split cycle and no global model. NECESSITY: exact at |D| = 2 — fidelity fails iff some split cycle is unbalanced in Harary's signed-graph sense. At |D| ≥ 3 it becomes graph colouring, and there is a theorem here rather than a slogan. Call a criterion CYCLE-LOCAL if it is a predicate on a cycle's own labels and site tags and nothing else, applied as 'some cycle of the federation satisfies P'. No cycle-local criterion is both sound and complete at |D| = 3: K₄ of ≠ split into three matchings fails fidelity, so completeness forces P on one of its 7 simple cycles — but every one of those cycles, re-presented alone with the same labels and sites, HAS fidelity, so soundness then fails. The argument does not run at |D| = 2, where an unbalanced cycle stays unsatisfiable when extracted from its federation, which is exactly why a cycle-local criterion exists there. ROUND 3 — four changes. (1) THE PROPERTY HAS AN EXACT CHARACTERIZATION: Γ has the gluing property iff the CORE of (D; Γ) is automorphism-transitive, from standard finite-CSP algebra — cores, endomorphism-invariance of pp-definable relations, pp-definability of orbits in a finite core. It is decidable in |D|^|D|, and when it fails the canonical conjunctive queries at two orbit representatives BUILD the refuting two-site federation. Novelty is not claimed; no exact prior-art search has been done. (2) THE BOUNDED SEARCH WAS HIDING A CASE: successor on a 6-path fails the property while the bounded violation search reports nothing at its default bounds, because the witness needs three auxiliary variables. A miss was never evidence and now demonstrably is not. (3) THE LOCALITY THEOREM GENERALIZES TWICE — no cycle-local criterion exists at ANY |D| ≥ 3 (K_{k+1} for every k), and no bounded-size local test of any fixed size s exists either: a graph of girth > s and chromatic number > k makes every ≤s-constraint sub-federation a forest while the whole fails, and Erdős 1959 supplies one for every (s, k). For |D| ≥ 3 a fidelity failure can be irreducibly GLOBAL. (4) THERE IS A SECOND ROUTE that needs nothing from Γ — exact separator projections on the block tree (36b). Witness: scripts/check-federation-invariants.mjs §4b, §7, §9.
cells.source: Proved here (block–cut induction). Neighbouring classical results: Beeri–Fagin–Maier–Yannakakis 1983 (local-to-global consistency on α-acyclic schemes) · Fagin 1983 (acyclicity degrees) · Harary 1953 (balance, |D|=2). NOT Freuder 1982, which assumes arc consistency the antecedent does not supply. Sheaf reading: Abramsky–Brandenburger 2011.
